audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] tells the player to "back away or Devour yourself if she pops it while you are already chunked".
audit.why: Tahm Kench cannot cast Devour on himself. Devour targets a champion — an enemy (only at three An Acquired Taste stacks) or an ally, whom it shields. There is no self-cast on any version of the ability. This is the single most dangerous line in the entry: it tells a player that at the exact moment Illaoi ults on them they have a panic button that does not exist, so they will stand in the field pressing R and die. The real self-save is Thick Skin's active, which converts the damage already banked into a shield.
audit.corrected: Back out and pop Thick Skin. Devour is for an ally or for her, never for yourself.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour: 'devours a champion... dealing magic damage if they are an enemy, or shielding them if they are an ally'; E Thick Skin active: 'Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield'

audit.whatIsWrong: Illaoi's passive is called "Cruel Tide" in wants.foe[2] ("Stack passive tentacles around the wave with Cruel Tide") and in late ("her Cruel Tide passive and Leap of Faith AOE").
audit.why: Cruel Tide is not an Illaoi ability and not a League ability. Her passive is Prophet of an Elder God. Worse, the invented name hides the mechanic that actually matters here: tentacles spawn only on nearby IMPASSIBLE TERRAIN. That single detail is the whole positioning rule of the matchup — fight in the open half of the lane and she has no ambient damage, fight against a wall and she has three tentacles. The current text ('around the wave', 'around a side lane') never tells the player where tentacles can and cannot appear.
audit.corrected: Prophet of an Elder God, and tentacles spawn on nearby impassible terrain — so the counterplay is to fight away from walls.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json — P 'Prophet of an Elder God': 'Illaoi and the Vessels she creates spawn Tentacles on nearby impassible terrain'

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says Test of Spirit forces you to "fight your own spirit under active tentacles or take the grievous wounds".
audit.why: Test of Spirit applies no Grievous Wounds and no healing reduction of any kind. What it actually does is rip out a spirit that echoes a percentage of the damage IT takes back onto you, and if the spirit is killed — or you walk too far from it — you become a Vessel that spawns tentacles of its own. Those are completely different threats with completely different counterplay: a Grievous Wounds framing tells a Tahm Kench player his Thick Skin healing is the thing at risk, when the real risk is that running away from the spirit is what converts him into a Vessel.
audit.corrected: Spirit echoes damage back to you; killing it or leaving it turns you into a tentacle-spawning Vessel. No Grievous Wounds involved.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json — E Test of Spirit: 'Spirits echo a percentage of the damage they take to the original target. If killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit, the target will become a Vessel and begin spawning Tentacles'

audit.whatIsWrong: Harsh Lesson is described four times as a leap or dash that 'triggers a tentacle slam', but the entry never says it is an auto-attack reset, and never gives its cooldown or range.
audit.why: Harsh Lesson is an auto-attack reset on a FLAT 4-second cooldown at every rank, at 400 range. Both facts change how a Tahm Kench plays the lane. The reset means the damage tell is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast — by the time you react to the cast the auto is already landing. The flat 4s means there is no 'wait out her W' window at any point in the game; the entry's repeated advice to trade after her cooldowns implicitly promises one.
audit.corrected: Name it as a 400-range auto-reset dash on a flat 4s cooldown at all ranks.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json — W Harsh Lesson: cooldown '4', range 400, flags dash + autoReset; _missing-interactions.json rule autoreset-burst-tell for tahmkench vs illaoi

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry warns that Illaoi is untargetable through the Leap of Faith slam.
audit.why: This is the flagged missing interaction for exactly this matchup, and it is decisive for Tahm Kench specifically: his commit is a single-target Tongue Lash that must land to stun. Throwing it into her R animation spends the one ability the whole matchup is built around and buys nothing. The correct read is to wait the slam out and stun her on the other side.
audit.corrected: Wait out the R animation rather than spending the stun into it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json — rule untargetable-dodges-burst, tahmkench vs illaoi: 'Illaoi can go untargetable through your commit (Leap of Faith (R)) — wait it out rather than spending everything into it'; champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json R flags include untargetable

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 plan in mid and late is built on "Abyssal Voyage" — "your own level 6 Abyssal Voyage is a roam tool and pressure valve" and "let Abyssal Voyage set up flank pressure on her".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not in the live kit. Tahm Kench's level 6 is Devour, which is not a roam tool at all and cannot be cast on Illaoi below three An Acquired Taste stacks. The flank tool he does have is Abyssal Dive (W), 1000-1200 range with a knockup on arrival.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated at three stacks; the flank/entry tool is Abyssal Dive and its knockup.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive (knockup, range 1000/1050/1100/1150/1200), R Devour, passive three-stack gate

audit.why: UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: the entry claims three times that Leap of Faith 'resets Harsh Lesson'. Riot's own R text in the kit says only that it damages nearby enemies and spawns a tentacle per champion hit — no reset clause — and I could not confirm the reset from the files available. I did not assert it is false; where I rewrote those sentences for other reasons I replaced the reset claim with the fact that Harsh Lesson's flat 4s cooldown means it is effectively always up anyway, which carries the same practical warning without asserting a mechanic I cannot verify.
sources: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json — R description contains no cooldown-reset clause; kit needsResearch block is empty (= unknown, not 'no')

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the most passive stretch — no ult, tentacles are accumulating around the wave, and a misplaced step into her field with even one passive tentacle nearby means a chunked HP bar she will immediately Harsh Lesson-follow. Use Tongue Lash to maintain your stack count from distance, shove the wave when she roams, and never fight her in the middle of three tentacles just to get a trade. Level 6 is hers: Leap of Faith spawns a ring of tentacles around her body and instantly resets Harsh Lesson — if she pops R while you are already low or mid-trade, you die inside the field. Respect the all-in threshold and back out; your own level 6 Abyssal Voyage is a roam tool and pressure valve, not a duel cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the most passive stretch — no ult, tentacles are accumulating on the walls, and a misplaced step into her field with even one passive tentacle nearby means a chunked HP bar she will immediately Harsh Lesson-follow. Use Tongue Lash to maintain your stack count from distance, shove the wave when she roams, and never fight her in the middle of three tentacles just to get a trade. Level 6 is hers: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit and her flat 4s Harsh Lesson is always up to chase — if she pops R while you are low or mid-trade, you die inside the field. Respect the all-in threshold and back out; your own 6 is Devour, and it needs three An Acquired Taste stacks on her first.

edits.before: Late game Illaoi becomes a split-push and teamfight monster if she has tentacles up around a side lane — her Cruel Tide passive and Leap of Faith AOE make grouped fights inside her field catastrophic for your team. Your job shifts to peel: keep your Devour ready to swallow your most valuable carry when Illaoi slams R in a teamfight, and use Tongue Lash to slow her out of your backline. You can still punish her in the open field away from tentacles with the 3-stack Devour combo, but never initiate on her inside an established tentacle zone. If she is ahead, do not 1v1 — pick off her tentacles, hover at the edge, and let Abyssal Voyage set up flank pressure on her.
edits.after: Late game Illaoi becomes a split-push and teamfight monster if she has tentacles up around a side lane — her Prophet of an Elder God passive and Leap of Faith AOE make grouped fights inside her field catastrophic for your team. Your job shifts to peel: keep your Devour ready to swallow your most valuable carry when Illaoi slams R in a teamfight, and use Tongue Lash to slow her out of your backline. You can still punish her in the open field away from walls with the 3-stack Devour combo, but never initiate on her inside an established tentacle zone. If she is ahead, do not 1v1 — pick off her tentacles and let Abyssal Dive knock her up from the flank.

edits.after: Illaoi's W (Harsh Lesson) comes online at 2 — a 400-range dash that resets her auto and pulls a tentacle slam with it, on a flat 4s cooldown, so fish Q stacks from outside that range.

edits.before: Your first clean punish window: if Illaoi misses E (Test of Spirit) and you have 3 An Acquired Taste stacks, Tongue Lash into Devour removes her from her own tentacle field entirely, wasting her cooldowns.
edits.after: Your first clean punish window: if Illaoi misses E (Test of Spirit) and you have 3 An Acquired Taste stacks, the Tongue Lash stun alone wastes her cooldowns — but Devour is not up until level 6.

notes: "Devour yourself" in spikes[2] is worth a targeted grep across the whole project — if the generator that produced this line did so anywhere else, every instance is a player being told they have a self-peel button that does not exist. Same for "Cruel Tide" as an Illaoi passive. Neither was caught by the packet's suspectNames detector, which only scores near-miss spellings of names that already exist in the kit and is blind to wholly invented names — that blind spot has now produced three separate classes of error in my slice (Abyssal Voyage, Cruel Tide, Devour-self).
